title: T1102 — Web Service
subtitle: Watch the full attack-and-detect story step by step.

steps.title: 1 · Infection in place
steps.caption: A phishing email earlier infected the workstation WKSTN-4417 with a small backdoor. The malware sleeps and waits for its fixed evening time.
steps.defender: no network signal yet; only the mail-gateway phishing report points at risk.

steps.title: 2 · Beacon to the paste site
steps.caption: The malware wakes and sends an HTTP request to the raw endpoint of a public paste site. This first touch is its beacon.
steps.defender: the proxy shows a non-browser process fetching a paste-site raw page - rare and worth a look.

steps.title: 3 · Dead drop decoded
steps.caption: The fetched page looks like random text but holds an encoded pointer to the real C2 server. The malware decodes it in memory. This is a dead drop resolver (T1102.001).
steps.defender: a plain text download on the wire; content inspection or EDR memory rules are the only ways to see the decode.

steps.title: 4 · Real C2 contact
steps.caption: The malware connects to the attacker-owned C2 server whose address it just learned.
steps.defender: EDR, proxy, and DNS all record a first-seen domain or bare IP from a workstation process.

steps.title: 5 · Command through a chat service
steps.caption: The operator hides an order in a post on a public chat or social platform. The malware polls the platform API and reads it.
steps.defender: a python-requests or curl user agent hitting a bot API endpoint from a workstation is a classic T1102.002 pattern.

steps.title: 6 · Local recon runs
steps.caption: The malware executes the ordered command: it lists files, reads system info, and packs the results as text.
steps.defender: EDR sees a suspicious parent-child chain - PowerShell spawning whoami, ipconfig, and net commands within seconds.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: 7 · Upload to the file host
steps.caption: The malware archives the collected files and uploads the archive to a public file hosting service for the attacker to collect later.
steps.defender: tens of megabytes of bytes-out to a personal file host - a top exfiltration signal for proxy and CASB rules.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: 8 · SOC correlates and contains
steps.caption: The SOC joins proxy, DNS, and EDR events into one timeline, blocks the abused services, and isolates the host.
steps.defender: one proxy hit is noise; proxy plus non-browser process plus recon commands is a case. Block, isolate, then hunt the same pattern fleet-wide.
